newsitem.title: GERMANY: Changeable weather disrupts German farm work.
newsitem.headline: Changeable weather disrupts German farm work.

text.p: Rainy weather interrupted German winter crop plantings as well as maize and beet harvests this week, the DWD meteorological office said in a report on Thursday.
"Fields are too wet to drive on in some regions and heavy machinery could cause damage to the soil structure," DWD wrote.
Barley, rye, and rapeseed were otherwise developing normally, with some winter wheat still waiting to be sown.
Maize and beet harvests suffered some delays but this was outweighed by progress made in recent weeks.
Lower Saxony's farm union said mild and sunny weather in the previous weeks had boosted beet yields and sugar contents.
Half of the leading sugar state's crop, which is forecast at seven million tonnes of beet, has already been harvested.
Sugar contents exceeded national averages at above 18 percent, the farm union said.
Lower Saxony accounts for a third of German sugar output.
DWD forecast rainy and cool weather in the week to Nov 13, having recorded eight to 15 degrees in the week to Nov 5, with South German spikes of 20 degrees.
